notes: The circuit image labels the breadboard rows f-j above the centre gap and a-e below it. I used the catalogue convention: bank 'b' is rows f-j and bank 't' is rows a-e. The LED and the top resistor legs are therefore in bank 'b', and the lower resistor legs and the pin wires are in bank 't'.
The LED legs are in columns 9-12, in the order R, common anode (longest leg), G, B. The longest leg is the second one, in column 10.
Each resistor spans the centre gap in columns 9, 11 and 12. The top leg is in row f and the bottom leg is in row e.
The 5V wire goes to column 10 in row f, the same strip as the LED common anode.
The text says '3 220 ohm resistors'. The schematic shows 220 ohm, so I used value=220.
The code comment says 'Anode: GND', but the circuit and text connect the common anode to 5V. I followed the circuit.
The Uno is powered and programmed over USB, which the manual does not show. I left the USB cable out of the graph.
